subject: math.MG
name: Symmetric Mahler conjecture
statement: For every origin-symmetric convex body K in R^n, is vol(K) vol(K°) at least 4^n/n!, where K° is the polar body?
importance: It predicts the sharp lower limit on the simultaneous size of a convex body and its dual.
status_note: The conjecture is proved in dimensions at most three and for many special classes; the general case in higher dimensions is open.

subject: math.MG
name: Nonsymmetric Mahler conjecture
statement: For every convex body K in R^n containing the origin in its interior, is vol(K) vol(K°) at least (n+1)^(n+1)/(n!)^2, the value attained by a suitably centered simplex?
importance: It predicts the universal sharp lower volume-product bound without symmetry assumptions.
status_note: Planar and various restricted cases are known; the assertion for arbitrary convex bodies in all dimensions remains open. The polar is taken about the stated interior origin.

subject: math.MG
name: Sharp order in Erdős’ distinct-distances problem
statement: Is there a universal c greater than zero such that every set of N at least two points in the Euclidean plane determines at least c N/sqrt(log N) distinct nonzero distances?
importance: It seeks the exact asymptotic extremal law for one of the foundational problems of combinatorial metric geometry.
status_note: Square-grid examples give order N/sqrt(log N); Guth–Katz proved a lower bound of order N/log N, leaving a logarithmic gap.

references.title: On the Erdos distinct distance problem in the plane

subject: math.MG
name: Hadwiger covering conjecture
statement: Can every convex body in R^n be covered by at most 2^n translates of smaller positive homothetic copies of itself?
importance: It is a basic sharp question about illuminating and covering convex bodies.
status_note: The smaller homotheties have scale strictly below one; the conjecture remains open in general, including dimension three.

subject: math.MG
name: Optimal sphere-packing density in four dimensions
statement: Is the D_4 lattice packing densest among all packings of congruent Euclidean balls in R^4?
importance: It is the next fundamental sphere-packing case after dimensions two and three.
status_note: The D_4 packing is optimal among lattice packings and the kissing number in dimension four is known; neither result proves global packing optimality.

subject: math.MG
name: Exact kissing number in five dimensions
statement: What is the largest number of nonoverlapping unit balls in R^5 that can all touch one fixed unit ball?
importance: It asks for the next unresolved local extremal configuration in Euclidean sphere geometry.
status_note: The four-, eight-, and twenty-four-dimensional kissing numbers are known; the exact five-dimensional value remains unresolved.

subject: math.MG
name: Equilateral-set conjecture for normed spaces
statement: Does every n-dimensional real normed space contain n+1 points whose pairwise distances are all equal?
importance: It asks whether every norm supports an analogue of a Euclidean regular simplex of full dimension.
status_note: Low-dimensional and special-norm cases are known; a general theorem for arbitrary finite-dimensional norms is still lacking.

references.title: Combinatorial distance geometry in normed spaces

subject: math.MG
name: Hadwiger–Nelson problem
statement: What is the least number of colors needed to color every point of the Euclidean plane so that points at distance one always receive different colors?
importance: It is a canonical meeting point of metric geometry, infinite graph coloring, and extremal combinatorics.
status_note: The chromatic number is at least five and at most seven; the unrestricted question is distinct from measurable-coloring variants.

subject: math.MG
name: Borsuk’s partition problem in four dimensions
statement: Can every bounded subset of R^4 with positive diameter be partitioned into five subsets each having strictly smaller diameter?
importance: It asks whether the classical diameter-partition principle survives in the first unresolved Euclidean dimension.
status_note: Borsuk’s conjecture holds in dimensions at most three and is false in sufficiently high dimensions; its four-dimensional case remains open.

subject: math.MG
name: Gromov’s filling-volume conjecture
statement: For n at least two, is the least volume of a compact Riemannian (n+1)-manifold filling the unit round S^n, without shortening any distance between boundary points, equal to the volume of a unit round hemisphere?
importance: It predicts a sharp metric-volume inequality whose extremizer is spherical geometry.
status_note: The boundary metric and non-shortening requirement are essential; the general higher-dimensional filling problem remains open.
